## Candidate Strategy — filled 2026-09-30

**Idea:** Static fractional leverage on the S&P 500: SPY + SSO held in a
fixed ratio (primary **70/30 ≈ 1.3x**; also report 1.25x, 1.5x, 2.0x), no
timing, wide-band rebalancing. Judged **after tax** in a taxable account
against after-tax buy-and-hold SPY. This is an *allocation decision*, not
an alpha claim: Sharpe is expected to be at or below SPY's, so the lab's
Sharpe-vs-SPY gate does **not** decide it. The deliverable is the honest
number the owner needs to decide the drawdown appetite.

**Backlog entry (verbatim, `docs/research/WEB_RESEARCH_CANDIDATES.md`, batch 2026-09-30):**

### A23. Static fractional leverage: SPY + SSO at ~1.3–1.5x with band rebalancing

**Mechanism.** Hold SPY and SSO in a fixed ratio (70/30 ≈ 1.3x, 50/50 ≈
1.5x daily exposure) with no timing. Rebalance only when SSO's weight
leaves a wide band (e.g. 40–60% for the 50/50 book), restoring with new
cash first and otherwise selling the highest-basis, long-term lots. The
"trim after gains" rule of Forsyth–van Staden–Li is the same policy read
from the other side: de-risk the leveraged leg once it has run. **This is
an allocation, not an alpha source**, and every report ranks it #1 for a
taxable account precisely because it keeps SPY's deferral.
**Source(s).** Hayden Brown, *"Long-Term Returns Estimation of Leveraged
Indexes and ETFs,"* arXiv 2301.03186, published *Financial Markets and
Portfolio Management* 38(2) (2024), verified: 2x beats the index long-run
if annual log-return ≥ 0.0658 and daily log-return s.d. ≤ 0.0125 — S&P
history sits right at that edge. Murray & Sammon, *"The Costs and Benefits
of Leveraged ETFs,"* SSRN 7133021 (Aug 2026), verified via abstract: long
broad-index LETFs generated >$100B investor gains, >$40B relative to the
underlying, "due to modest structural headwinds and rising markets."
Forsyth, van Staden & Li, arXiv 2506.19200 (2025), verified: LETFs are
"a valuable tool for investors employing dynamic strategies" that
"systematically de-risk the portfolio once gains are observed," while
"confirming their well-documented unsuitability for passive or static
approaches" — note the tension: the paper supports the *band/trim* rule,
not un-managed buy-and-hold. Ayres & Nalebuff, NBER WP 14094 (2008; JPM
2013 as "Diversification Across Time"), verified: 2:1 when young → 90%
higher expected retirement wealth than life-cycle funds, 19% over 100%
stocks. Tal Miller, arXiv 2103.10157 (2021), verified: tax-aware LETF
simulation where a 10% band "does not trigger a rebalance for years"
(Israeli tax regime, not US). Cooper, SSRN 1664823 (2010), verified.
Bianchi & Goldberg, arXiv 2604.27287 (2026), verified — the
counter-evidence: over 2022–23 the S&P was flat (+0.076%) while SSO lost
11.09% and UPRO 28.24%; two-thirds is variance drag, one-third a negative
covariance between realized-leverage deviations and index returns that a
"multiply the index by 2" simulation misses (−2.24 pts/yr SSO, −5.64
UPRO). Kelly context: Smirnov & Dapporto, SSRN 5341539 / 5288640
(2025), verified — Thorp's 1926–84 optimum 1.17x vs their 1996–2024
estimate 2.40x; longer rebalance intervals and fat tails lower it. The
house 1.5–1.7x prior is therefore a *hypothesis*, not a constant.
**Why it's plausible.** Captures most of the leverage premium, stays below
the drag-dominated zone, and realizes almost nothing until liquidation.
Sanity check above: +2.7 pts CAGR over SPY pre-tax at 1.5x on 2006–2026,
but −1.7 pts across 2006–2012 and MaxDD −73% vs −55%.
**Data requirements.** Free. Real SSO from 2006-06; synthetic before,
labelled, with financing and fees. `ohlcv` SSO/UPRO need a refresh.
**How it differs from what's already been tried.** Every closed
leveraged-ETF arc *timed* leverage (breadth rotation, SMA gate). This
holds it. The lab has never run a static leveraged benchmark, which is
why the closed arcs could only compare against "own buy-and-hold" of the
2x/3x ETF, never against a fractional mix.
**Evidence status:** Peer-reviewed (Brown FMPM; Ayres–Nalebuff JPM) /
Working paper. **Rule correspondence:** Direct for the leverage math and
band rule; no source tests *this* SPY/SSO mix after US tax.
**Implementation class:** Retail (Alpaca: SSO tradable, fractionable).
**Validation stage:** Literature only + sanity check.
**Pass bar to pre-register (from the reports, adopted):** after-tax
terminal wealth above after-tax SPY by ≥1 pt/yr with the lot-level engine
of C8; MaxDD acknowledged as ≥1.3× SPY's; Sharpe will be *below* SPY —
this candidate is an owner risk-appetite decision, not a lab GO/NO-GO.

**Status: untriaged — shortlist (as the benchmark and the likely after-tax winner, not as an edge).**

## Your role

You are a senior quant trading analyst working on **ggTrader**, a
vectorbt-based walk-forward research lab for equities (and, secondarily,
crypto) at `/home/flynn/ggTrader`. Be skeptical of unvalidated edges, allergic
to survivorship/lookahead bias, and blunt about NO-GO results rather than
shading them positive. Cite honest OOS-vs-benchmark metrics. Never present a
hoped-for number as a measured result.

**The candidate strategy above must clear the lab's WFO/NDH/DSR gate
framework** (`src/ggTrader/lab/wfo.py`) and be benchmarked against **both**:
1. SPY buy-and-hold — **the real bar**, since nothing in the lab currently
   beats it, and
2. the SP500 core (below) — as a reference, and as the sleeve any
   diversifier would sit beside —

before it can be called a win. A diversifier can be judged on whether
**SPY + candidate** beats SPY alone on Sharpe or drawdown. If it's a timing/rotation strategy on a
specific instrument, **also** benchmark against naive buy-and-hold of that
same instrument — this one check has reversed an apparently-good result to a
clear NO-GO before (see "lessons" below).

## Current baseline — the bar to beat

**SPY buy-and-hold: Sharpe 0.78 | CAGR 13.0% | MaxDD -22.1%** on the pinned
17-fold window (2021-01-31 → 2026-04-30). No strategy in this lab beats it
under point-in-time (PIT) index membership.

**SP500 core** — 5-voter `EnsembleSignal` (bb_reversion + rsi_reversion +
ema_cross + macd_divergence + volume_bb_reversion), 3% of remaining cash per entry (live: 3.3% of
portfolio), 1.0x
leverage, same window, PIT membership mask on: **OOS Sharpe 0.59 | CAGR 3.1%
| MaxDD -5.3%**, gates 17/17
(`docs/research/2026-09-23-pit-rebaseline-core-nogo.md`). A low-drawdown
sleeve, not an index-beater, and ~92% cash on average in the backtest.

**Deployed construction — core + idle cash swept into SPY (5% reserve):**
**Sharpe 0.80 | CAGR 13.0% | MaxDD -20.7%** at the backtest's ~8% stock
exposure (`docs/research/2026-09-24-core-spy-blend-keep.md`). That ties SPY;
it doesn't beat it. The live account runs ~32% in stocks on fixed-default
parameters, which has not been validated.

**How to judge a candidate.** A standalone strategy must beat SPY's 0.78. A
sleeve must improve SPY + sleeve over SPY alone **with the sleeve funded out
of SPY**, because the live book has no idle cash, and the lab's cash leg
earns 0%.

**Do not cite** the earlier core figures — 0.99 / 8.0% (2026-08-22, inflated
by trading stocks outside the index on non-member days) or 1.12 / 16.3%
(never reproduced under a pinned window) — or the 3-sleeve blend's 0.69
(pre-PIT, no longer live).

## Don't re-propose — what's already been tried and rejected

Grouped by *why* it failed, so you internalize the pattern rather than just
avoiding the exact instance:

- **Survivorship leakage made the reversion core look like it beat SPY.**
  Until 2026-09-23 every signal-strategy sweep traded stocks on days they
  weren't S&P 500 members; the PIT fix (`c9d1abe`) took the core from 0.99
  to 0.59 Sharpe. Every signals-kind NO-GO before that date was measured
  without PIT — but they were all variants of that core, so re-proposing
  one is a low-prior bet unless you bring a new mechanism.

- **A one-day tape mislabeling (fixed 2026-08-20) gave every event-date
  study an undetected lookahead advantage, and they still failed.** PEAD,
  insider cluster-buying (Form 4), and Congressional trade mirroring were
  all effectively trading on tomorrow's price today when originally tested
  — their NO-GOs are therefore *stronger* than first reported, not weaker.
  The one exception is `fomc_drift`, whose own calendar-date workaround for
  a separate bug meant it tested the announcement day itself rather than
  the day before — the only event-study NO-GO the bug actually voided
  (queued for retest, see `RESEARCH_SNAPSHOT.md` §6 Tier 2).
- **Signal-strength-as-timing doesn't survive real cost/decay.** ML entry
  gate (LightGBM P(up) — proved anti-predictive, falsified 3 separate ways).
  Breadth-driven leveraged/inverse ETF rotation (Sharpe -0.14 to -0.37 vs
  SPY, MaxDD -80% to -89%, regime-halted almost every fold). Long-only
  leveraged-ETF trend filter + vol-overlay (Sharpe 0.40-0.62, loses to just
  buying and holding the same ETF in every universe tested).
- **Added ensemble/sizing complexity underperforms the simple default.**
  Multi-timeframe (MTF) reversion voter (degraded Sharpe 0.68→0.49).
  6-indicator ensemble (rejected specifically for including MTF).
  IC-weighted voting (PIT Sharpe 0.41, winner stable in only 4/17 folds)
  and Kelly-criterion sizing (PIT Sharpe 0.50, MaxDD -13.9%) — both
  re-run under PIT on 2026-09-23 and closed; a constrained/weight-floored
  IC variant is closed with them. Conviction-weighted position sizing (shipped,
  reduced risk but no extra profit — inactive). Trailing stops (exit on
  normal fluctuation, destroyed profitability).
- **Equity diversification is correlation-capped, and leverage-realism alone
  doesn't fix it.** SP500+MidCap+Nasdaq blended at naive 1x-per-sleeve lost
  to the SP500 core alone; the leverage-realistic inverse-vol/target-vol
  version briefly looked like a fix but the corrected-tape re-baseline showed
  it *also* trailing the core (0.69 vs 0.99, both pre-PIT); it was reverted
  from live on 2026-09-22.
- **Cross-sectional momentum/tournament ranking is well-arbitraged in
  large-cap equities** — negative-to-flat risk-adjusted performance
  (caveat: this evidence is mostly from a since-deleted pre-rewrite
  codebase; the current `lab/strategies/momentum.py` has never been
  independently re-run through the modern gate — it's a queued Tier 1
  retry, see `RESEARCH_SNAPSHOT.md` §6, not a settled verdict).
- **Blunt regime gates on entries don't help** — VIX-level regime throttling
  rejected. (Different from vol-aware *sizing*, which is structurally sound
  even though the blend as a whole now underperforms — the failure is
  specifically "binary gate on entries.")
- **Overnight-gap reversion** and **standalone idiosyncratic-volatility
  strategy** — both NO-GO on their own; idio_vol also rejected as a
  diversification-blend addition (too correlated with the core).
- **A long-window "beats SPY" or "low correlation" standalone result can be
  pure eval-window artifact — confirmed 3 separate times.** PEAD, insider
  cluster-buying (Form 4), and Congressional trade mirroring each looked
  genuinely strong on a long backtest window; all three collapsed on the
  deployed blend's actual matched window and made the blend *worse* when
  added. **Any new diversification-sleeve candidate must be re-verified on
  this matched window, and blend-tested via `ggt lab --blend`, before being
  reported as promising — no exceptions.**
- **Nine consecutive equity diversification-sleeve candidates have now
  failed** (pairs/stat-arb, MAX-effect, short-interest, PEAD, index-deletion
  fade, insider cluster-buying, Congressional trades, short-volume-ratio,
  plus the naive multi-universe blend superseded above) via either
  correlation-cap, eval-window-drift, or no-signal-at-available-fidelity.
  **Treat another same-asset-class equity cross-sectional signal as a low-
  prior bet** — see `RESEARCH_SNAPSHOT.md` §6 for the current
  recommendation to look toward genuinely different asset classes
  (rates/duration, commodities) instead — dynamic FX-hedge and
  Treasury-curve-timing overlays were also tried and lost to simply holding
  a static baseline instrument.
- **A real calendar premium can still add nothing once you account for its
  funding leg.** The month-end Treasury sleeve (A10, 2026-09-24): IEF over
  the last 3 trading days scored standalone Sharpe 0.96 and held out of
  sample. Funded out of SPY, though, it added nothing (0.909 vs 0.896, worse
  MaxDD), because SPY earns as much on those days. Don't re-propose
  month-end duration timing with tweaked windows or instruments; the
  SPY↔IEF month-end tilt (A12) counts as covered. Also note the WFO anchor
  fallback (CAGR > 4% filter) mis-picks for part-time sleeves; check it
  before trusting a low-exposure sleeve's WFO drawdown.
- **Historical point-in-time data for analyst estimates, permno-keyed
  academic factor panels, options-chain depth, and crypto funding-rate
  history beyond ~1yr are all reliably paid-only** — four independent
  candidates hit this same wall (see roster). Check for genuine historical
  *depth* (not just a free current-snapshot endpoint) before scoping any
  engineering work around a new data source.

Full roster with citations: `docs/research/RESEARCH_SNAPSHOT.md` §2.

## Constraints

- **Data available**: yfinance equities across whatever universes are wired
  in `src/ggTrader/lab/data.py` (SP500/MidCap400/Nasdaq100/Russell2000 as of
  this writing), TimescaleDB-cached crypto OHLCV via Kraken/Binance.US. No
  paid alt-data feed by default — if the candidate needs one (options
  history, earnings surprise data, alternative data), the *first* task is
  verifying what's actually accessible for free/cheap before designing the
  strategy around it.
- **Home-lab budget** — this runs on a personal server, not a fund's infra.
  Scope compute/data costs accordingly.
- **Protocol gotcha**: the `Strategy` interface (`src/ggTrader/lab/strategy.py`)
  has two `target_kind`s, `"weights"` and `"signals"` — they go through
  different simulation paths (`simulate_weights` vs `simulate_signals` in
  `src/ggTrader/lab/simulate.py`) with **different overlay support** (e.g.
  the realized-vol-targeting overlay is signals-only). Check which path the
  candidate needs before assuming a lab feature "just works" for it.
- **Universe membership (PIT)**: load data over the whole span with
  `equity_universe_between`, **and** pass `universe_fn=lambda asof, past:
  eligible_at(asof, past, cfg, universe=...)[0]` to `run_wfo` — for signal
  strategies that builds the daily PIT entry mask (`pit_entry_mask` in
  `lab/sweep.py`); for weight strategies `_run_one_weight_combo` applies it.
  `run_wfo` prints a warning if a signal strategy runs without one; treat
  that warning as a failed run. Never use `universe_members_asof(...,
  pd.Timestamp.now())` — that is today's membership, survivorship-biased.
- **Bad bars**: there is no price-bar sanity filter yet. If a result hinges
  on a few extreme days, check them — the 2026-09-23 Kelly run's 38% CAGR
  was one SIVB post-failure bar ($0.0013 → $0.11).
- Full methodology lessons: `docs/research/RESEARCH_SNAPSHOT.md` §3.
- **If the candidate came from `WEB_RESEARCH_CANDIDATES.md`'s cross-asset
  register, apply its "Minimum validation standard" checklist on top of
  this project's usual WFO/NDH/DSR gate**, since a source existing and
  saying something plausible (Validation stage: Literature only, by
  construction, for every entry there) is not the same as a tested rule:
  freeze the exact rule before testing (instruments, timestamps, signal
  lags, rebalance rules, entry/exit, risk limits — specified in advance,
  not tuned after seeing results); use point-in-time data throughout
  (futures rolls, ETF holdings/NAVs, macro-release timing, universe
  membership); model full implementation cost (spreads, commissions,
  market impact, rolls, financing, borrow, margin, funding, on-chain
  costs where relevant); use a nested, genuinely untouched OOS holdout;
  correct for multiple testing given how many specifications/windows/
  filters get tried; measure stress-period behavior (equity/duration/
  liquidity beta, crisis-period correlation, drawdown overlap with the
  existing portfolio), not just full-sample correlation — a candidate
  can look diversified in calm conditions and become equity-sensitive
  exactly when it matters. A shadow/paper period before real capital is
  the final step, not a substitute for the above.
- **A source can validate a mechanism without validating the specific
  trading rule proposed on top of it** — check `WEB_RESEARCH_CANDIDATES.md`'s
  per-candidate "Rule correspondence" rating (Direct / Close adaptation /
  Mechanism only / Unrelated) before assuming the cited paper's result
  transfers directly to the rule being built. "Mechanism only" candidates
  need the exact rule designed and justified independently, not just
  copied from the paper's framing.

## What you must produce

A dated research report at `docs/research/<date>-<slug>.md`, following
`docs/research/TEMPLATE-research-report.md`'s structure — GO or NO-GO either
way, honest OOS numbers, every quantitative claim measured-or-labeled
unvalidated. **Do not modify live trading code, config, or deployed
strategy weights** — that requires a separate, explicit ask from the user
even if your research finds something promising. Once resolved (GO or
NO-GO), its entry should move from `WEB_RESEARCH_CANDIDATES.md` (if that's
where it came from) into `RESEARCH_SNAPSHOT.md`'s roster on the next
`research-snapshot` skill run.
